title: The Contact of Geneva
premise: Casper Amberdale has spent six years as a ghost inside a financial-crimes unit, laundering nothing and tracing everything, living in a safe house so bland it barely exists. When the property is listed online with interior photos — his books, his coffee cup, his life — he realizes someone sold his invisibility to flush him out. Following the listing's digital trail, Casper uncovers a laundering network he once helped dismantle quietly reassembling under new names, with a final transaction designed to trigger an 'accidental' gas explosion at a Geneva banking summit that would erase both evidence and witnesses, including the analyst who first flagged the listing: Mara Voss, the woman he once loved and abandoned for duty. Racing from Zurich to Geneva, Casper must choose between burning his own cover to save her or preserving the case that defines him; in the end he exposes the plot publicly, sacrificing his anonymity forever but finally belonging — to Mara, and to a life no longer hidden.
about_author: Gideon Thornbury is a former compliance auditor who spent a decade inside the gray corridors of international finance before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about people who vanish into systems, and what it costs them to come back.

chapters.title: The House That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: POV Casper. A routine morning shatters when Casper finds his safe house listed on a real-estate site, complete with photos of his private rooms. He reports it internally and is told to stand down. Emotional beat: the cold dread of realizing someone has been watching, and that his own agency may already know.

chapters.title: Clean Money, Dirty Hands
chapters.summary: POV Casper, with a flashback interlude. Reviewing his caseload, Casper notices small anomalies in dormant accounts — money moving in patterns he recognizes as his own old methodology, weaponized. His supervisor dismisses him. Emotional beat: professional pride curdling into paranoia as he suspects an insider is mirroring him.

chapters.title: Mara
chapters.summary: POV alternating Casper/Mara. The listing's metadata traces to a shell company once flagged by analyst Mara Voss — the woman Casper loved and abandoned six years ago to protect her. He watches her from across a Zurich tram platform, unable to approach. Emotional beat: longing sharpened by guilt; love as the one liability he never wrote off.

chapters.title: The Buyer's Agent
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Posing as a prospective buyer, Casper contacts the listing agent and finds a dead man's identity behind the brokerage license. In the agent's office he photographs a floor plan of the summit venue in Geneva annotated with ventilation routes. Emotional beat: the hunt ignites; fear transmutes into purpose.

chapters.title: What the Photos Sold
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Mara, investigating the same shell company, realizes the listing was bait meant to draw out whoever recognized the interiors — meaning the network knows Casper is alive and where. She breaks protocol to warn him, and they meet for the first time in six years. Emotional beat: reunion charged with anger, relief, and unfinished love.

chapters.title: Six Years of Silence
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Holed up together, they reconstruct the network's structure over one long night — and their history. Casper confesses why he vanished: the last man who got close to him died in a car crash dressed up as bad luck. Emotional beat: intimacy rebuilt on shared danger; duty and desire openly at war.

chapters.title: The Accident Calendar
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Decoding the ventilation annotations against the summit schedule, Mara pinpoints the date and method: a gas-line 'failure' timed to the closing dinner, insured heavily through the very accounts Casper once froze. They have seventy-two hours. Emotional beat: ticking-clock urgency; the horror of murder disguised as paperwork.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper goes to his director with proof and is offered a deal: stay silent, keep his cover, let the agency handle it quietly — a handling he can see will fail. He refuses, burns his identity by sending the full dossier to three journalists. Emotional beat: the irrevocable choice; grief for the self he is destroying.

chapters.title: Geneva, Closing Dinner
chapters.summary: POV alternating Casper/Mara. Infiltrating the summit as catering contractors, they race the saboteur through service corridors as the gas begins to flow. Casper confronts the insider — his own former mentor — and forces the shutdown minutes before detonation, taking a knife wound doing it. Emotional beat: climax; terror, fury, and the strange calm of finally acting as himself.

chapters.title: A Name in the Window
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Recovering in a Geneva hospital, Casper watches news coverage name him openly for the first time in six years. The safe house sells; he doesn't care. Mara sits beside him holding two coffee cups, and he lets himself be seen. Emotional beat: resolution; inheritance of a real life, love chosen over duty, belonging earned.
